## rebar-debug final report — landed & merged

**Problem.** `last_pass.publish`'s 3-attempt CAS-publication retry loop slept on a
FIXED, UNJITTERED schedule `(0.1, 0.2)[attempt]`, so colliding reconciler passes woke
in lockstep and re-collided (thundering-herd).

**Proven root cause.** `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/last_pass.py:343`. Runtime
probe (always-colliding `_cas_advance`): two independent passes both slept
`[0.1, 0.2]` byte-for-byte → lockstep. Same probe proved the OTHER half is already
correct: `old_oid` fed to each attempt was the fresh re-read value `['aaa','bbb','ccc']`,
so line 344 re-reads after the sleep → NO staleness defect (matches the ticket's
scoping; no surprise). Legitimacy: `defect` (violates the non-lockstep design invariant
from merged baldish `_cas_backoff` + the Jira DC transport jitter idiom + this AC).

**Defect origin (`caused_by`).** `git log -L 343,343` / `git blame -w` → commit
`fe5a447061cd` "Add durable bridge status and canary witness", a `new file` that
introduced the unjittered schedule as written (not a carrier). Its trailer →
**b69c-5787-81b8-4052**. Independently verified as DISTINCT from baldish's origin
`ebee`/freeborn-dizzy-raven (that touched `push_classify.py`; this is a separate
lineage — the file was born with the schedule unjittered). Close class `plan_defect`,
`--caused-by=b69c-5787-81b8-4052` recorded on the close.

**Test (RED→GREEN, held out, teeth).** New held-out unit oracle
`tests/unit/test_last_pass_backoff_jitter_paediatric.py` drives two colliding
publications through the real `publish`; asserts each delay ∈ `[base, 1.25*base]` and
the two passes' sequences are NOT byte-identical (lockstep), with a zero-contention
negative control. Confirmed RED first (`assert [0.1,0.2] != [0.1,0.2]`); GREEN after
the fix (which the blind fixer never saw); mutation teeth: re-seeding the fixed
schedule returns it to RED (run in an OS sandbox). The existing integration backoff
test was retargeted from the exact `[0.1,0.2]` schedule to the jitter window (count +
escalation preserved).

**Fix.** Added `import random`, `_CAS_BACKOFF_JITTER = 0.25`, and
`delay = base * (1.0 + random.random() * _CAS_BACKOFF_JITTER)` — the merged baldish
idiom exactly. Base schedule, staleness re-read, retry count, and `LastPassError`
escalation all unchanged. stdlib only, no new dependency.

**Scope & safety.** Caller-dependency sweep: the delays are internal to `publish`; no
caller depends on the exact values (only the existing integration test, updated).
Restoration not creation; no new dependency; no test weakened (the integration
retarget was a required contract update, teeth moved to the held-out unit oracle).

**Step-7 siblings.** None. Construct axis: the only member of the "unjittered backoff
between competing CAS/ref-lock writers" class besides this was baldish's
`push_classify._cas_backoff` (already jittered). `_ref_lock.py` `_cas_advance` sites
are single-shot (no retry-backoff loop); `access_check` JQL poll and
`retry.py`/`acli_rest.py` are single-client transport/poll retries (non-writer-
contention, same class as recorded non-sibling `_TRANSPORT_BACKOFF_SECONDS`);
`dispatch_apply_phases`/`generation`/`resign`/Jira-DC 429 already jittered. Parity
axis: `publish` is the single CAS-publish core → N/A. Recorded non-siblings
re-confirmed, not re-filed.

**Residual risk.** None observed beyond the swept class.

**Replication.** The integration test drives the real `reconciler sync` entry point
through the actual CAS push loop and now observes jittered backoff — the report's
scenario no longer reproduces.

**Landing.** Gerrit change **2366** (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2366),
`LLM-Review +1` + `Verified +1`, submitted and MERGED to `origin/main` as
`be177e212ebf`.
